body.statement:
For every \(a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm G}\), use a normalized quasi-uniform spline basis of degree sufficient for \(C^s\) approximation and a growing dimension satisfying
\[
J_n\to\infty,
\qquad
\sqrt n\,J_n^{-2s}\to0,
\qquad
\frac{J_n^{\alpha_a}}{\sqrt n}\to0,
\qquad
\frac{J_n^{\alpha_a+1}\log n}{n}\to0,
\qquad
J_n^{-s}\log(n/J_n)\to0,
\]
with \(\alpha_a=0\) under the bounded-support convention.  Uniformly over gamma-separated \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm S}\) obeying these schedules, the data-driven clip is inactive with probability tending to one when the propensity is bounded away from zero and is first-order negligible otherwise, and
\[
\sup_P P_P\!\left[
\max_{\substack{a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm G}\\ \tau\in\mathcal T}}
\left|
\sqrt n\{\widehat q_a(\tau)-q_{a,P}(\tau)\}
-\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\mathrm{IF}_{a,P}(O_i;\tau)
\right|>\varepsilon
\right]\longrightarrow0
\]
for every \(\varepsilon>0\).  If \((L_{a,P})_{a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm G}}\) denotes the Gaussian subvector in \(\text{def:moving-row-law}\), then
\[
\sup_P d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(
\mathcal L_P\!\left[
\left\{\sqrt n\bigl(\widehat q_a(\tau)-q_{a,P}(\tau)\bigr)\right\}_{a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm G},\tau\in\mathcal T}
\right],
\mathcal L_P\!\left[(L_{a,P})_{a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm G}}\right]
\right)\longrightarrow0.
\]
The covariance blocks are \(E_P[\mathrm{IF}_{a,P}\mathrm{IF}_{a',P}^{\top}]\).  In particular, for each fixed \(P\) in the scheduled domain the displayed lawwise asymptotic linear expansion and joint Gaussian limit hold.
body.justification: The likelihood Riesz projection produces the learned-propensity score contribution, while Hall tails and the bounded-propensity Hölder branch verify uniform Lindeberg rather than assume it.
body.gap: Regular QTE theory does not provide this finite-inverse-moment profiled-sieve expansion with the data-driven clipping rule, a uniform asymptotic remainder, and row-specific Gaussian approximation.
body.consumer: It supplies the regular coordinate and shared cross-arm covariance in mixed and two-Gaussian moving row laws.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a finite-variance arm and write \(q_{a,P}\), \(f_{a,P}\), and \(\mathrm{IF}_{a,P}\).  Let \(L_{a,P}\) be centered Gaussian with covariance
\[
\Sigma_{a,P}=E_P\!\left[
\{\mathrm{IF}_{a,P}(O;\tau)\}_{\tau\in\mathcal T}
\{\mathrm{IF}_{a,P}(O;\tau)\}_{\tau\in\mathcal T}^{\top}
\right].
\tag{G1}
\]
All suprema below are over the explicitly scheduled gamma-separated Gaussian domain in the statement.

For a log-propensity direction \(g\), direct differentiation of the Bernoulli log likelihood gives
\[
s_g(O)=\frac{\{\mathbf1(A=a)-\pi_a(X)\}g(X)}{1-\pi_a(X)},
\qquad
\mathcal I_{a,P}(g_1,g_2)=E_P\!\left[
\frac{\pi_a(X)}{1-\pi_a(X)}g_1(X)g_2(X)\right].
\tag{G2}
\]
The derivative of the signed functional in direction \(g\) is
\(\dot\Lambda_{a,P}(g)=E_P\{m_{a,\tau}(X)g(X)\}\).  Its information-space Riesz representer is
\[
r_{a,\tau,P}(X)=m_{a,\tau}(X)\frac{1-\pi_a(X)}{\pi_a(X)},
\tag{G3}
\]
because substituting (G3) into (G2) gives
\(\mathcal I_{a,P}(r_{a,\tau,P},g)=\dot\Lambda_{a,P}(g)\).  Positivity licenses the divisions, and
\[
E_Ps_{r_{a,\tau,P}}^2
=E_P\!\left[m_{a,\tau}(X)^2\frac{1-\pi_a(X)}{\pi_a(X)}\right]
\le C_{\mathrm G}
\tag{G4}
\]
by \(\text{ass:finite-variance}\) and \(|m_{a,\tau}|\le1\).

Let \(r_{a,\tau,P,J}\) be the information projection of (G3) on the likelihood sieve.  On the cell at distance of order \(j/J\) from the endpoint, \(\text{ass:boundary-link}\), the local support and normalization of the B-splines, and \(\text{ass:holder}\) give, after summing the cellwise powers,
\[
\|s_{r_{a,\tau,P,J}}-s_{r_{a,\tau,P}}\|_{L^2(P)}=o(1)
\tag{G5}
\]
uniformly when \(2<\gamma_{a,P}<\infty\), equivalently \(0<\alpha_{a,P}<1\).  The same calculation and the likelihood score equation yield
\[
\sqrt n\,|\text{product approximation bias}|\le C\sqrt nJ_n^{-2s},
\qquad
\sqrt n\,|\text{reciprocal quadratic remainder}|
=O_P(J_n^{\alpha_{a,P}}/\sqrt n),
\tag{G6}
\]
and empirical-Hessian replacement error
\[
O_P\!\left\{\frac{J_n^{\alpha_{a,P}+1}\log n}{n}\right\}^{1/2}=o_P(1).
\tag{G7}
\]
Every term is \(o_P(1)\) by the displayed schedules.  If \(\gamma_{a,P}=\infty\), then \(\pi_a=\exp(g_a)\) and the fixed Hölder radius gives \(\inf_x\pi_a(x)\ge e^{-C}>0\).  Profiling the additional \(\log d_a\) direction against the quasi-uniform spline space gives a residual of squared norm \(O(J_n^{-1})\), a profiled coefficient error \(O_P(\sqrt{J_n/n})\), maximum sample residual \(O_P\{\log(n/J_n)\}\), and profiled spline-function supremum error
\[
O_P\!\left\{\sqrt{J_n\log J_n/n}+J_n^{-s}\right\}.
\tag{G8}
\]
Thus \(J_n\log n/n\to0\) and \(J_n^{-s}\log(n/J_n)\to0\) give uniform sample-point consistency.  This is the profiled argument already established for the bounded arm in \(\text{prop:finite-variance-sanity}\), with constants uniform over the fixed Hölder ball.

For each fold, (G2)--(G8), the likelihood score equation, and the nonpositive inner product of a concave maximizer's feasible displacement with its normal-cone residual give
\[
\sqrt n\sum_{k=1}^K\frac{|I_k|}{n}
\int m_{a,\tau}(x)
\frac{\widehat\pi_{a,-k}(x)-\pi_a(x)}{\pi_a(x)}\,dP_X(x)
=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n s_{r_{a,\tau,P}}(O_i)+o_P(1).
\tag{G9}
\]
The coefficient is one because every observation is used in \(K-1\) training folds, each of size \(n(K-1)/K+O(1)\).  Conditional on a training fold, cross-fitting makes the centered evaluation error mean zero, and its conditional variance is at most
\[
C\int\frac{(\widehat\pi_{a,-k}-\pi_a)^2}{\pi_a}\,dP_X
=O_P(J_n^{-2s}+J_n^{2\alpha_{a,P}}/n)=o_P(1).
\tag{G10}
\]
For finite \(\gamma_{a,P}>2\), the last conclusion uses \(2\alpha_{a,P}<\alpha_{a,P}+1\); the bounded case uses \(\alpha_{a,P}=0\).

Clipping is first-order negligible.  In the bounded case, (G8) and the common lower bound make it inactive with probability tending uniformly to one.  For finite \(\gamma_{a,P}>2\), introduce only for this proof \(b_{a,P,n}^{\circ}=\vartheta_a/h_{a,P,n}\).  The definition of \(t_{a,P,n}\) and \(\text{ass:hall}\) give \(h_{a,P,n}=(c_{a,P}n)^{1/\gamma_{a,P}}\{1+o(1)\}\); Hall integration then gives
\[
\sqrt n\left|E_Pm_{a,\tau}(X)
\left\{\frac{\pi_a(X)}{\pi_a(X)\vee b_{a,P,n}^{\circ}}-1\right\}\right|
\le Cn^{1/2-(\gamma_{a,P}-1)/\gamma_{a,P}}=o(1)
\tag{G11}
\]
uniformly because \(\gamma_{a,P}\ge2+\epsilon_\gamma\).  Its centered version has variance tending uniformly to zero because Stieltjes integration of \(\text{ass:hall}\) gives
\[
E_P\!\left[\pi_a(X)^{-1}\mathbf1\{\pi_a(X)\le u\}\right]
\le Cu^{\gamma_{a,P}-2}.
\tag{G12}
\]
The count sandwich proves \(\widehat b_{a,n}/b_{a,P,n}^{\circ}\to_P1\) when \(\vartheta_a>0\); when \(\vartheta_a=0\), both thresholds vanish.  This transfers (G11) to the empirical clip.

Applying the exact algebraic identity
\[
\rho_\tau(e-v)-\rho_\tau(e)
=-v\{\tau-\mathbf1(e\le0)\}
+\int_0^v\{\mathbf1(e\le s)-\mathbf1(e\le0)\}\,ds
\]
with \(v=t/\sqrt n\), and using \(\text{ass:conditional-density-modulus}\) and \(\text{ass:quantile-density}\), gives the uniform local expansion
\[
\widehat Q^{\mathrm G}_{a,n,\tau}(t)
=\frac12f_{a,P}(\tau)t^2
-t\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n
\left[
\frac{\mathbf1(A_i=a)\psi_{a,\tau}(Y_i)}{\pi_a(X_i)}
-s_{r_{a,\tau,P}}(O_i)
\right]+o_P(1).
\tag{G13}
\]
By (G3), the bracket is exactly
\[
m_{a,\tau}(X_i)+\frac{\mathbf1(A_i=a)
\{\psi_{a,\tau}(Y_i)-m_{a,\tau}(X_i)\}}{\pi_a(X_i)}
=f_{a,P}(\tau)\mathrm{IF}_{a,P}(O_i;\tau).
\tag{G14}
\]
It is centered by consistency, unconfoundedness, and
\(E_P\psi_{a,\tau}\{Y(a)\}=0\).

It remains to verify the uniform Gaussian approximation.  Since \(\mathcal T\) is finite, (G14), the density lower bound, and \(|m|,|\psi|\le1\) reduce multivariate Lindeberg to the inverse-weight term.  For finite \(\gamma_{a,P}\ge2+\epsilon_\gamma\), (G12) with \(u=x^{-1}\) gives
\[
E_P\!\left[
\frac{\mathbf1(A=a)}{\pi_a(X)^2}
\mathbf1\{\pi_a(X)^{-1}>x\}\right]
=E_P\!\left[\frac1{\pi_a(X)}\mathbf1\{\pi_a(X)<x^{-1}\}\right]
\le Cx^{-(\gamma_{a,P}-2)}\le Cx^{-\epsilon_\gamma}.
\tag{G15}
\]
For \(\gamma_{a,P}=\infty\), the common propensity lower bound makes the summands uniformly bounded.  Taking \(x\) proportional to \(\sqrt n\) proves uniform Lindeberg.  For each fixed coefficient vector, expand the characteristic function of its scalar projection to second order on the Lindeberg-truncated event; the remainder is bounded by the corresponding truncated second moment.  Gaussian smoothing followed by removal of the smoothing converts the resulting characteristic-function approximation into bounded-Lipschitz approximation to the centered Gaussian having row covariance (G1).  No covariance convergence across rows is needed.

Finally, the common lower curvature in (G13) and a two-sided convexity comparison at the quadratic minimizer imply, uniformly over arms and \(\tau\),
\[
\sqrt n\{\widehat q_a(\tau)-q_{a,P}(\tau)\}
=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\mathrm{IF}_{a,P}(O_i;\tau)+o_P(1).
\tag{G16}
\]
The preceding Lindeberg calculation and (G16) prove both uniform assertions in the replacement statement.  Dropping the suprema yields its fixed-law corollary.
